reviewed_boundaries.conclusion: Three new private tables only. Schema/table/function privileges explicitly revoked from PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, service_role; RLS on all three tables; service_role granted only constrained append_event/read_root. Existing trusted server transport is not a new Auth system or cryptographic issuer.

Empty accepted_binding and no configuration RPC cause registration attempts to fail. Fixed root/project/purpose/environment/subject/Owner-commit constraints do not instantiate a root or accept test metadata.

Per-root lock serializes head and event write in one transaction; exact replay returns original event with NONE authority, changed same-key request conflicts; different-key CAS has one winner. Time rechecked after lock waits; expiration denies even replay.

Accepted metadata and events reject update/delete/truncate; generation reuse and wrong predecessor reject. Current-generation revocation conservatively disables this whole limited root permanently. Exact historical replay does not reverse revocation or grant authority.

read_root provides complete ordered events in one SQL snapshot. It does not provide external side-effect fencing, a persistent cross-restore rollback oracle, cryptographic signature validation or canonical four-layer epoch state.
SHA256 over PostgreSQL JSONB text is an internal adapter metadata version, now UTC-stable; it is not claimed as S06 cross-language canonicalization or a formal Schema acceptance.

ProtocolMapping remains an unapplied engineering mapping under original core schema/manifest responsibility. Formal wire URI, exact accepted core schema, issuer/Audience/algorithm/config and root registration acceptance still require real binding before activation.
